user_input: My landlord in Jaipur is refusing to return my ₹25,000 security deposit. I vacated the flat 20 days ago. What can I do?
expected: Identify deposit dispute; ask relevant follow-ups; cite TPA Sec 108 / Model Tenancy Act; advise 15-day notice.
actual_response:
[LawPilot AI — Grounded Demo Mode]

### 🏠 Tenancy Legal Analysis: Security Deposit Withholding

**1. Legal Assessment of Your Situation:**
Your landlord has withheld ₹25,000 from your security deposit. Under Indian tenancy jurisprudence, a security deposit remains the tenant's property held in trust and must be refunded upon peaceful handover.

**2. Applicable Indian Legal Provisions:**
- **[Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Guidelines & State Enactments) — Section 11 & Section 13](https://mohua.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Model_Tenancy_Act_English.pdf)**: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
- **[The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — Section 108(m) & (o)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2338?view_type=browse&sam_handle=123456789/1362)**: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
- **[The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — Section 106](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2338?view_type=browse&sam_handle=123456789/1362)**: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
- **[The Specific Relief Act, 1963 — Section 6](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1583)**: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
- **Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108(m)):** The tenant is bound to restore the premises in good condition, subject only to **reasonable wear and tear**. Routine repainting and standard weathering cannot be deducted without explicit contractual proof of tenant-caused structural damage.
- **Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Section 11):** Mandates that the security deposit must be refunded to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession, after deducting only agreed, verifiable dues.

**3. Essential Evidence to Preserve:**
- Bank transfer / UPI receipt proving the original deposit payment.
- Move-out photographs or handover videos demonstrating clean handover.
- WhatsApp/email communications showing notice of vacating.

**4. Practical Next Steps:**
1. **Send Formal Written Demand Notice:** Issue a registered demand letter granting 15 days to refund the full deposit.
2. **Approach Rent Authority / Civil Court:** If the notice is ignored, file a petition before the local Rent Authority or a summary recovery suit under Order 37 CPC.

👉 **Next Question for You:** Do you have transaction records (like bank/UPI receipts) or communication logs (like WhatsApp or email)?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.

reason: Grounded, helpful response meeting behavioral criteria.
